before: pdf opens a headless file graphics device; plot sends drawing commands to the active device. dev.off closes it and finalizes the PDF. A function with on.exit(dev.off(), add = TRUE) makes cleanup occur even if plotting fails.

The fixture creates one synthetic scatterplot in plot.pdf. main is its title; xlab and ylab are axis labels; pch chooses a point symbol. No GUI display, browser execution or publication is implied. Check the generated artifact rather than treating printed success as visual verification.

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r
draw <- function() {
  pdf("plot.pdf", width = 5, height = 4)
  on.exit(dev.off(), add = TRUE)
  plot(1:3, c(2, 4, 3), main = "Synthetic study points",
       xlab = "Session index", ylab = "Minutes", pch = 19)
}
draw()
cat(file.exists("plot.pdf"), "\n", sep = "")

```
Expected output or behavior: TRUE. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

before.question: If the y-axis label changes to Seconds without converting the values, what changes?
choices: Only the label; the numbers are not converted to seconds.
Every plotted value is multiplied by 60.
before.explanation: Axis text documents intended units but performs no unit conversion; changing it alone can mislabel the data.

after.question: If the label changes from Minutes to Seconds, are the numbers converted?
choices: Yes. Every number is multiplied by sixty.
Yes. The points move by themselves.
after.explanation: Changing a label does not perform a unit conversion.
